item.title: Slovenia Strips Ex-Premier of Immunity for Police Purge Probe
item.description: Slovenian lawmakers stripped former Prime Prime Minister Robert Golob of his immunity to let prosecutors probe allegations he meddled in a police overhaul at the start of his tenure in 2022.

item.title: Modi’s Developed Nation Goal Remains on Track, Top Official Says
item.description: India’s economy can approach $20 trillion by 2046 if it continues growing at its current pace, a top government official said, putting it in reach of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s goal of becoming a developed nation.

item.title: India’s ONGC Reviews Assets in Venezuela After US Green Light
item.description: A team from the international investment arm of India’s Oil & Natural Gas Corp. has arrived in Venezuela to review assets in the country, according to people familiar with the matter, weeks after the company received a green light from the US.

item.title: Renault-Backed Wandercraft Seeks €100 Million in New Funding
item.description: Wandercraft, the French robotics startup backed by Renault SA, is seeking about €100 million ($116 million) in fresh funding to expand its business, people with knowledge of the matter said.

item.title: Germany on Track to Grow by as Much as 1%, Nagel Tells Le Monde
item.description: Germany’s economy could expand by 1% this year, twice the pace projected only three months ago, Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel told Le Monde.

item.title: Shadow Lenders in India Line Up Over $1 Billion in Rupee Bonds
item.description: India’s shadow lenders are set to raise at least 100 billion rupees ($1.1 billion) through the issuance of local-currency bonds as early as next week, according to people familiar with the matter, as they race to lock in borrowing costs before they rise further.

item.title: Turkey’s $75 Billion Hot-Money Boom Creates Policymaker Dilemma
item.description: A surge of money into Turkish lira assets is creating a dilemma for policymakers, who are weighing how to curb speculative short-term flows without choking off an important source of support for the currency.

item.title: Yen Gains After BOJ Hawk Leaves Door Open for Outsized Hike
item.description: The yen strengthened against the dollar after Bank of Japan Board Member Hajime Takata, one of the bank’s most hawkish members, left the door open for an outsized interest-rate increase as well as back-to-back hikes.

item.title: Global Bonds Are Slumping But It’s Nothing Like the 2022 Wipeout
item.description: The selloff sweeping global bond markets looks painful, but it’s nothing compared with the rout four years ago, when soaring inflation forced central banks into a series of rapid-fire interest-rate hikes.

item.title: Vietnam’s Vingroup Plans Debut Won Bond After Shares Hit Record
item.description: Vietnamese conglomerate Vingroup JSC is in discussions with brokerages about selling its first bond denominated in the Korean won, according to people familiar with the matter, as the company seeks to broaden its investor base after its shares hit a record.

item.title: Nagel Signals ECB Will Hike Next Week, Cautious Beyond That
item.description: Governing Council member Joachim Nagel indicated that the European Central Bank will raise borrowing costs next week, though he stayed wary on what comes after that.

item.title: Nordea More Upbeat on Nordic Growth Over Efficiency, Tax Breaks
item.description: Nordea Bank Abp raised its economic forecasts for most of the Nordic region through next year due to better-than-expected resilience to higher energy prices, geopolitical tensions and global trade disruption.

item.title: Woolworths’ New CEO Bets More on Food in Retailer’s Overhaul
item.description: Woolworths Holdings Ltd. is reorienting its business around its upmarket South African food operations, putting its best-performing division at the center of the group as new Chief Executive Officer Sam Ngumeni plans to direct a larger share of investment toward the unit.

item.title: Homeplus Creditors Vote to Accept Korean Mart’s Turnaround Plan
item.description: Creditors of South Korean megamart Homeplus agreed on Wednesday to accept a rehabilitation plan aimed at keeping the company afloat.

item.title: Biggest Thai Fund Sees More Gains for Banks, Data-Center Plays
item.description: Thailand’s dividend-paying banks and developers riding the data-center boom are attractive options for investors seeking shelter from bouts of selling in other markets, according to the nation’s largest private money manager.

item.title: AI Data Center Spending to Reach $32 Trillion by 2050, PwC Says
item.description: Global data center spending is set to reach $31.6 trillion through 2050 to meet the world’s growing appetite for AI, an investment boom with no precedent in history, according to PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP.

item.title: India’s Diaspora Deposit Flows Surpass $100 Billion, FE Reports
item.description: Inflows under the Reserve Bank of India’s special overseas deposit facility have topped the $100 billion mark, the Financial Express newspaper reported Wednesday, citing officials it did not identify.

item.title: Minimax Emerges as Mainland China Investors’ New Favorite Stock
item.description: Minimax Group Inc. became the most popular Hong Kong-listed stock among mainland Chinese investors last month, in the latest sign of the latter’s voracious appetite for the country’s new-generation AI model developers.

item.title: Copper’s Rally Stalls as Worries About Global Economy Resurface
item.description: Copper fell for a second day, dropping with other metals, as resurgent oil prices fanned concerns about prospects for the world economy.

item.title: Nvidia Partner Gets Strong Demand for Rare GPU-Tied Loan in Asia
item.description: GMI Cloud, an Nvidia Corp. partner, secured commitments for more than double the amount it was seeking in a loan backed by the sale of computing power from advanced chips, underscoring strong demand for one of the first such deals in Asia.

item.title: Rupee Rally Gets a Boost From Bullish Charts and RBI’s Reserve Ammo
item.description: However, a continued increase in oil prices may dent optimism around the currency.

item.title: Unitree Plunges 50% From Peak in Fast Reversal After Huge Debut Pop
item.description: Unitree Robotics shares have tumbled 50% from their intraday peak, marking one of the steepest declines for a newcomer on Shanghai’s Star Board.

item.title: RBNZ Delivers Back-to-Back Rate Hikes to Curb Inflation
item.description: New Zealand’s central bank raised its key interest rate for a second straight meeting, aiming to shift to less stimulatory settings in an effort to head off inflationary pressures.

item.title: BOJ Board Hawk Calls for Nimble Hikes to Prevent Price Risks
item.description: Bank of Japan Board Member Hajime Takata, one of the bank’s most hawkish members, reiterated his call for nimble interest rate hikes to prevent upward price deviations, adding to growing speculation over a near-term policy move.

item.title: Australian Economy Beats Estimates, Adding to Rate-Hike Case
item.description: Australia’s economic growth unexpectedly accelerated last quarter, adding to the case for the Reserve Bank to raise interest rates again as inflation remains stubbornly strong.

item.title: Insolvent Bathla Faces 24-Hour Deadline for Deal With Creditors
item.description: Insolvent Australian property developer Bathla Group faces a 24-hour timeframe for talks with its creditors to secure short-term funding, according to a person familiar with the matter, in its last-ditch effort to avert collapse.

item.title: China Bond Sales Set to Accelerate, Putting Focus on PBOC
item.description: China’s government bond sales are expected to pick up after a lull as authorities seek to boost a sluggish economy, with increased issuance likely to prompt the central bank to inject more liquidity.

item.title: AI Startup Cognition Set to Raise Around $1 Billion at a $47 Billion Value
item.description: Artificial intelligence coding startup Cognition AI Inc. is set to close a new round of funding that would vault its valuation to about $47 billion, according to people familiar with the efforts.

item.title: Nvidia Nears $14 Billion Hugging Face Deal This Week
item.description: Nvidia Corp. is in advanced talks to acquire artificial intelligence startup Hugging Face in a transaction that may total about $14 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: BOJ’s Ueda Hints at September Rate Hike as Bets on Move Mount
item.description: Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda hinted that a rate hike is likely when the board convenes for a meeting later this month, saying that officials will decide on policy with upside price risks in mind.
